spatial_entity.notes: Analytical regional target for the mid-first-millennium BCE state-transition zone; not a single polity.

claim.summary: Specialist scholarship on the transition from lineage societies to states in the middle Ganga valley identifies slavery as emerging alongside new settlement, social segmentation, urbanization and state formation. This supports a regional practice claim without implying a slave-society economy or uniform conditions across every polity in the valley.

territorial_practice.notes: P2 reflects a specialist regional interpretation of an emerging/recurrent institution. It does not imply that enslaved labour dominated the agrarian economy.

source.title: The Transition to State
source.independence_notes: Specialist reconstruction of social and political change in the mid-first-millennium BCE Ganga valley.
source.reliability_limitations: Regional synthesis; slavery is one element within a broader state-formation argument and does not provide a census or polity-by-polity prevalence estimate.

version.version_label: From Lineage to State, Oxford Academic chapter page

source.title: Hindus Beyond the Hindu Kush: Indians in the Central Asian Slave Trade
source.independence_notes: Independent historical synthesis discussing the long chronology of slavery in South Asia.
source.reliability_limitations: The article's main focus is later India/Central Asia; its ancient discussion is contextual rather than a dedicated reconstruction of the middle Ganga valley.

version.version_label: Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society 12.3 (2002)

geometry.resolution_method: The evidence target is an analytical middle-Ganga transition zone spanning several evolving polities; no single defensible polygon is assigned.
